one_liner: A George Mason University staff role recruiting prospective graduate students through outreach, info sessions, events, and applicant follow-up.
fit_summary: Daniel's outgoing, relationship-building style and comfort with the public match the core of a recruitment coordinator role, and consulting work for government clients shows professional client-facing experience. The posting has no description, so it's unclear whether GMU wants prior higher-ed admissions or CRM experience, which Daniel may lack. It's also a university staff job rather than a policy or emergency-management role, so Daniel should weigh how well it fits a government career goal.
eligibility: The full posting text isn't available; open the jobs.virginia.gov link or GMU's careers site (jobs.gmu.edu) to confirm the minimum qualifications.
Check whether a bachelor's degree is required, which is typical for university recruitment coordinator roles.
Confirm the closing date; it is listed as open until filled or not stated, so the posting could close without notice.

strategy: Before applying, read the full description at the posting URL or on jobs.gmu.edu and replace these generic keywords with the exact phrases it uses.

Frame your IEM experience around stakeholder engagement, such as coordinating with government clients, organizing meetings or trainings, and communicating with diverse audiences, using only duties you actually performed.
Lead with people skills backed by concrete examples: events you staffed, presentations you gave, and relationships you built and maintained.
Mention any connection to GMU or its policy programs (for example, the Schar School); your policy knowledge helps you speak credibly to prospective MPP or MPA students.
Write a short cover letter if allowed, and apply quickly because open-until-filled postings can close early.
State-system and university applications don't fall under the federal two-page rule, but keep the resume tight anyway, around 1-2 pages.

How would you track and follow up with a large pool of prospective applicants?
